findings.title: Lint check reads the project but writes to a target root that may not be the project
findings.description: `writeOrSuggest` writes to `path.join(this.ctx.targetRoot, rel)`, but the lint *detection* reads from `this.ctx.projectRoot`. The bash original had the same split (`PROJECT_ROOT` for reading, `TARGET_ROOT` for writing), and the module docstring explicitly documents that intent ("Reads the project from projectRoot and writes to targetRoot"). But the new cf call sites always pass `projectRoot === targetRoot` (`installCheckout` in `packages/cli/src/commands/setup-ide.ts:88-100`), so the split is dead in production while remaining live in the dry-run path — where `targetRoot` is the sandbox. The consequence is that in a dry run the lint check reports on the real project but writes nothing to the sandbox, so `--dry-run --write-lint` will not show `ruff.toml` / `eslint.config.mjs` as an added file, and the dry run's diff will under-report what `--write-lint` would create. `packages/cli/src/ideInstall/dryRun.ts:103-117` copies `LINT_WRITE_PATHS` into the sandbox specifically to make this comparison work, so the sandbox copy is prepared and then never written to. Either the lint writer should target the sandbox in dry-run mode, or the dry-run report should account for lint writes; today the two are inconsistent.

findings.title: `lint/python/ruff.toml` baseline does not exist in the shipped guide
findings.description: `LintCheck.python()` calls `fs.readFileSync(this.source('python', 'ruff.toml'))` when no ruff config exists, but the vendored guide at `project-documents/ai-project-guide/project-guides/lint/python/` contains only `required` — there is no `ruff.toml`. The guide's own bash script has the same read (`lint_write_or_suggest python ruff.toml "$LINT_SOURCE_DIR/python/ruff.toml"`), so the guide ships without it too, but the guide's `readme.setup-ide.md` documents `lint/python/ruff.toml` as the Python baseline. In cf this path throws `ENOENT` from `fs.readFileSync`; `installIde` catches it as a filesystem error (`packages/cli/src/ideInstall/installer.ts:59-66`) and returns `exitCode: 1`, so `cf setup-ide` on any Python project without a ruff config fails with a raw ENOENT message rather than the intended "no ruff.toml — run setup-ide with --write-lint" suggestion. The test suite only passes because `packages/cli/tests/ideInstall/fixture_guide/lint/python/ruff.toml` exists in the fixture but not in the real guide, and the `realGuide.test.ts` smoke test uses the `agents` target against the real guide — where the project has no `pyproject.toml`, so the Python branch never runs. This is exactly the "test fixture must include the actual format that parser will consume in production" rule from AGENTS.md: the fixture has a file the shipped guide lacks.

findings.title: Worktree installs lose the stale-file prune the deleted propagation path performed
findings.description: The removed `propagateToWorktrees` pruned worktree files that a previous guide version installed but the new one no longer ships, using the worktree's own `.context-forge/<target>.manifest` as the baseline. The new `installWorktrees` loop calls `installCheckout` per worktree, which does run `InstallManifest.finish()` — but `finish()` reads `this.oldManifest`, i.e. the manifest inside the worktree's own root (`packages/cli/src/ideInstall/manifest.ts:118-122`). Since each worktree previously received a byte copy of the root's manifest under the old propagation path, this should work for worktrees installed by a pre-slice cf. However, for worktrees that never received a manifest copy (installed by a guide older than v0.19.0, or created after the last root install), `oldManifest` is absent and `finish()` falls back to `LEGACY_MANIFEST_ENTRIES` only — so files the guide dropped between versions stay in the worktree indefinitely. This is the same gap the deleted code explicitly closed via `rootBaseline` (the pre-run root manifest snapshot) joined to the worktree's own manifest. The new code has no equivalent: `setupIdeAction` no longer snapshots the root manifest before the install, and `installWorktrees` passes only `guideDir`. The behavior difference is not covered by any test — `packages/cli/tests/commands/worktreePrune.test.ts` was deleted wholesale and no replacement exercises the manifest-driven prune in a worktree.

findings.title: Deleted worktree-prune and generated-prompt-sweep coverage was not replaced
findings.description: `worktreePrune.test.ts` (373 lines) was deleted with no equivalent added. It covered `pruneStaleFiles` (edited-file retention, containment/escape rejection, symlinked-directory containment, non-regular files, empty-dir removal depth) and `sweepGeneratedPrompts` (marked vs. unmarked files, empty-dir removal), plus end-to-end propagation with manifest carry-over. The new `packages/cli/tests/commands/worktreePropagation.test.ts` shrank to 50 lines covering only `propagationTargets` filtering. The containment/symlink protections were explicitly security-relevant (the old `pruneStaleFiles` had `escapesLexically` and `realpathSync` guards against deleting outside the worktree); with the code deleted there is no live path that needs them, but the corresponding manifest-driven prune in `InstallManifest.finish()` (`packages/cli/src/ideInstall/manifest.ts:126-149`) now performs deletions in worktrees and has no test for the edited-file retention case (`⚠️ Kept <rel>: ... edited since`) or for a path that escapes the target root. `packages/cli/tests/ideInstall/manifest.test.ts` lost its `readManifest`/`parseManifestLine` suites entirely, and no new test covers `finish()`'s prune branch.

findings.title: `parseRulesExclude` does not trim, but the bash script did
findings.description: `parseRulesExclude` splits on `,` with no trimming, and the validator rejects entries with surrounding whitespace — so the two are consistent for values that pass validation. The bash `rule_is_excluded` did trim each pattern (`pattern="${pattern#"${pattern%%[![:space:]]*}"}`), so a hand-edited `.context-forge.toml` containing `rules.exclude = "dart.md, swift*.md"` would work under bash but is rejected by cf's validator and will not match under the new installer. The validator's comment still says the consumer "matches each pattern literally (bash `case` glob rules)", which is accurate for the new installer, so this is a deliberate tightening rather than a bug — but the config description and error message do not tell a user upgrading from the bash flow that a previously working value is now rejected. Worth a note in the changelog for `rules.exclude` consumers.

findings.title: `readRulesExclude` throws a plain `Error` for a non-string config value
findings.description: `readRulesExclude` raises `new Error(...)` when `rules.exclude` resolves to a non-string. `ConfigManager.get` already types the value as `string | boolean | number`, so a boolean or number in a hand-edited TOML reaches this branch. A plain `Error` surfaces through `handleError` as `Error: rules.exclude resolved to a boolean, expected a string` with no stack, which is acceptable, but a `UserError` would match the surrounding convention (every other expected-failure path in this file throws `UserError`). Note also that `readRulesExclude` is called once per checkout inside `installCheckout`, so a worktree with a malformed config aborts the whole run with a stack-shaped message rather than being recorded as a per-worktree failure.

findings.title: Target model remains single-sourced and the removed capability-probe scaffolding has no dangling references
findings.description: The descriptor table now drives validation and the managed-marker check only, with `propagateDirs`/`generatedPromptDirs` removed along with `guideScript.ts`. A grep across `packages/` for `runSetupIdeInWorktrees`, `execSetupIde`, `guideSupports`, `readCapabilities`, `setupIdeScriptPath`, `GuideCapability`, `propagateDirs`, and `generatedPromptDirs` returns no remaining references, so the deletion left no dead imports or orphaned exports. The `Record<Target, TargetDescriptor>` annotation still makes an unhandled target a compile error, and `normalizeTarget` remains the single alias resolver used by both `setup-ide.ts` and `init.ts`.
